performance_tasks.brief: A mapwork task (10 marks): a map extract given as a markdown grid of squares with their features, heights and a scale, and 1-mark parts on the key, a six-figure grid reference, a compass direction and a bearing, a distance along a route, a height difference, relief and drainage.
performance_tasks.objective_ids: choose 2-4 objectives from this topic that the task genuinely exercises

performance_tasks.brief: A second mapwork task (10 marks) on a different landscape (upland and river if the first was coastal or urban), with a cross-section described point by point and settlement pattern and communications.
performance_tasks.objective_ids: choose 2-4 objectives from this topic that the task genuinely exercises

performance_tasks.brief: A graph and table task (8 marks): data from one theme to plot on the learner's own paper, a trend to describe with figures, a calculation, and a reason to suggest.
performance_tasks.objective_ids: choose 2-4 objectives from this topic that the task genuinely exercises

performance_tasks.brief: A photograph and diagram task (6 marks): a described photograph or field sketch of a landscape to describe, with features to identify and a reason to suggest.
performance_tasks.objective_ids: choose 2-4 objectives from this topic that the task genuinely exercises

performance_tasks.brief: A third mapwork task (10 marks) on an urban or coastal extract: land use, urban morphology, services and functions of settlements, communications, with grid references and bearings.
performance_tasks.objective_ids: choose 2-4 objectives from this topic that the task genuinely exercises

performance_tasks.brief: A second graph and table task (8 marks) on a different graph type (a population pyramid, a climate graph, a triangular or scatter graph): read values, describe the pattern, calculate a range or percentage, suggest a reason.
performance_tasks.objective_ids: choose 2-4 objectives from this topic that the task genuinely exercises

performance_tasks.brief: A third graph and table task (8 marks) on a map-based resource (a choropleth map, a flow diagram or a dispersion graph): extract information, describe the distribution, suggest a suitable graph for data given.
performance_tasks.objective_ids: choose 2-4 objectives from this topic that the task genuinely exercises

performance_tasks.brief: A fourth mapwork task (10 marks) on a rural extract: drainage density and stream patterns, relief described with suitable terms, a route distance, a bearing, and inferences about land use from the map evidence.
performance_tasks.objective_ids: choose 2-4 objectives from this topic that the task genuinely exercises

ao_mix_note: The syllabus states its AO weights as a share of MARKS, so planned_ao_mix_by_marks is the one that answers "does this resource match the exam". It values each card at the tariff of the question it models, split across the AOs the card declares, and values each performance task at the marks of the paper part it models. The count-based mix below is reported only because it is what a reader expects to see; do not balance against it. AO shares by ITEM COUNT: Every objective needs one recall anchor, so AO1 has a structural floor of about 24% in this topic (36 objectives against 153 slots) and cannot reach the 30% target by count however many other cards are added - padding the bank to chase it makes the resource worse. The framework already measures the AO4 share in practice time rather than by count for the same reason. Treat AO1 above target as expected, and AO2/AO3/AO4 below target as the thing worth fixing.
